hubIntro: Mount Juliet is known as the City Between the Lakes, with Old Hickory Lake to the north and Percy Priest Lake to the south. Providence Marketplace, the big retail center on Providence Parkway, sits at the heart of it, surrounded by subdivisions, with older farmland and wooded lots still holding on at the edges along Mount Juliet Road, Lebanon Road and the lakeshores.

Triple Oak Services is based in Nashville and travels to Mount Juliet for tree removal, tree trimming and pruning, stump grinding, storm damage cleanup and land clearing. This page covers what tree work in Mount Juliet tends to involve, how fast growth has shaped the local tree problems, and what to know before you hire a crew. Every job starts with a free, no-obligation estimate.

sections.h2: Fast growth, new subdivisions and the trees left behind
paragraphs: Mount Juliet is one of the fastest-growing cities in Middle Tennessee, and a lot of its housing went up in the last couple of decades. Communities like Lake Providence, Willoughby Station, Baird Farms, Herrington, Saddle Ridge and Wright Farms were built on land that was graded, cleared and replanted, which leaves a specific set of tree problems. Builders plant fast-growing, inexpensive trees close to foundations and driveways, and young trees that were never structurally pruned can develop weak, V-shaped crotches that split in wind.

Trees saved from the original woodland during construction often struggle for years afterward. Their roots were cut, compacted or buried, and a tree that looked fine at closing can decline and die a few years later. Dead trees standing close to a house, a fence or a playset are one of the most common reasons homeowners here call us. The sooner they come down, the lower the risk and cost.

sections.h2: Older Mount Juliet: Hickory Hills, Mount Juliet Road and the lake roads
paragraphs: Away from the new subdivisions, older parts of town have established trees that have had decades to grow. Neighborhoods like Hickory Hills and the streets off Mount Juliet Road and Lebanon Road have mature oaks, maples, hickories and cedars that overhang roofs, power service lines and driveways. Their crowns build up dead wood and their roots lift driveways and sidewalks, so trimming and selective removal are common calls.

Properties near the shorelines of Old Hickory Lake and Percy Priest Lake face extra wind and wet soil. Trees leaning toward the water, trees with exposed roots and trees with sudden crown dieback are the ones we are most often asked to look at. Trees close to the water's edge on lake property can also be affected by lake-management rules, so check before cutting near the shoreline.

sections.h2: Weather and the signs a tree is failing
paragraphs: Spring thunderstorms and straight-line winds are the main cause of storm damage in Mount Juliet. Saturated soil lets roots lose their grip, and summer drought stresses trees so they drop dead limbs in later storms. Young trees on newly graded lots often have small root systems and are the first to lean or fall after heavy rain.

Watch for a lean that is getting worse, cracks in the trunk or where a big limb meets it, mushrooms or conks around the base, soil heaving on one side and large dead branches high in the crown. Any of these is a reason to have the tree inspected before the next storm.

sections.h2: Before you remove a tree in Mount Juliet
paragraphs: Whether you need approval depends on the property. Many Mount Juliet subdivisions have HOAs with rules on removing trees, development approvals can include tree plans, and trees near the shoreline can be affected by federal lake rules. Check with the City of Mount Juliet and your HOA before removing a large tree, and confirm current requirements since they can change.

Look up before work starts. Trees touching or close to power lines should be handled by the utility or a qualified line-clearance crew, and anyone in danger should call 911. If stump grinding or digging is involved, call Tennessee 811 so buried utilities can be marked. We point out lines, fences, septic fields and structures when we quote.

We are a locally owned, licensed and insured company. For Mount Juliet jobs we give a free estimate, explain how the tree will come down and what the price includes, remove it safely and haul the debris away. Stump grinding can be added on the same visit, and storm damage and emergency removal are available when a tree is already down. If trimming will do the job, we will tell you.

tree-trimming-pruning.title: Tree Trimming & Pruning in Mount Juliet, TN | Triple Oak Services
tree-trimming-pruning.description: Tree trimming and pruning in Mount Juliet, TN: dead limb removal, crown thinning, structural pruning for young trees, clearance from roofs and lines. Call 615-561-0472.
paragraphs: In a city that has grown as fast as Mount Juliet, trimming is about two things: setting young trees up right and managing older ones. Young trees in newer communities like Herrington, Saddle Ridge and Lake Providence often benefit from structural pruning so they grow with one strong leader instead of splitting in a storm.

Mature trees in older areas near Mount Juliet Road and Hickory Hills build up dead wood and spread over roofs, chimneys and driveways. Thinning the crown and removing dead and crossing branches reduces weight, lets wind pass through and keeps branches off siding and gutters.
We do not top trees. We explain what will be removed and why before any cutting begins.

faq.q: When should I start pruning a newly planted tree?
faq.a: Structural pruning is usually most helpful in a tree's first several years. We can look at what you have and tell you what it needs.

faq.q: Can you trim branches over my roof?
faq.a: Yes. Limbs over roofs and gutters are among the most common trimming calls. Limbs near power lines should be handled by the utility or a qualified line-clearance crew.

paragraphs: A stump left behind after a removal makes mowing, fencing and landscaping harder. We grind stumps below grade in Mount Juliet so the spot can be filled, seeded or sodded, whether it is a small stump in a new subdivision yard or a large hardwood stump on an older lot near Lebanon Road.

In newer neighborhoods, irrigation lines, invisible dog fences and buried utilities run close to where trees were planted, so the job needs a look first. Call Tennessee 811 before any digging or grinding so buried utilities are marked, and we will go over access, depth and cleanup during the estimate.
Stump grinding pairs well with removal. Ask us to grind the stump on the same visit.

faq.q: Do you grind stumps near irrigation lines?

faq.q: Can I plant grass where the stump was?
faq.a: Yes. We grind below grade so the spot can be filled with soil and seeded or sodded.

A typical job removes brush and undergrowth, takes out the trees in the way, grinds stumps if needed and leaves a clean, usable site. We walk the property first so we know what stays and what goes, then give you a clear price before work begins.
If clearing is part of a build, check with the City of Mount Juliet or Wilson County about any permits or approvals the project needs. We clear to the lines you mark.
